newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN MINISTER DI RUPO TO STAY ON - SPOKESMAN.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN MINISTER DI RUPO TO STAY ON - SPOKESMAN.

text.p: Belgian deputy prime minister Elio di Rupo will remain in his function while the country's top court investigates allegations that he had sex with under-age boys, Di Rupo's office said on Thursday.
"Mr. Di Rupo remains in function, absolutely," his spokesman Bart Cammaerts told Reuters.

A Belgian parliament commission early on Thursday recommended that the Cour de Cassation investigates sex charges against Di Rupo and make a report to parliament by December 9 at the latest. Parliament is set to vote on the recommendation at 1400 local (1300 GMT).

The spokesman said it was not clear what the extent of the court's powers in the investigation were. He said it was clear that Di Rupo would be heard by the court, but added he did not know whether the court's mandate included a possible confrontation with the main witness in the case.
Belgian media began on Thursday to question the reliability of the witness whose testimony formed the basis of a report on Di Rupo by the Brussels public prosecutor to the parliament.
Several newspapers the man's statements were contradictory and that he had a history of inventing stories and even identities.
Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene earlier on Thursday declined to make any comment about Di Rupo.
Dehaene will answer questions from parliamentarians after they vote on the commission's recommendation.
Several commission members belonging to the four parties which make up the four-party centre-left coalition government said they thought Di Rupo could stay on -- at least for the moment.
